titre: La scénariste de Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, a quitté Sandfall Interactive en juillet dernier
chapo: ActuGaming.net La scénariste de Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, a quitté Sandfall Interactive en juillet dernier Célébré dans le monde entier pour tout un tas de qualités, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 […] L'article La scénariste de Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, a quitté Sandfall Interactive en juillet dernier est disponible sur ActuGaming.net
extrait: Célébré dans le monde entier pour tout un tas de qualités, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 aura aussi marqué pour son récit et sa narration, tous les deux prisés par une partie du public. Une grande part de cela est à attribuer au travail de Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, qui est la scénariste principale du jeu et qui a aidé Sandfall à donner vie aux aventures de Maelle, Verso et compagnie. Pendant que le studio travaille sur son prochain projet, on apprend que cette fois-ci, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen ne fera pas partie de l’aventure. On ignore encore sur quoi Sandfall Interactive est en train de travailler après le succès de Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, mais cela se fera sans Jennifer Svedberg-Yen. Dans une interview accordée à GamesBeat, on apprend que l’intéressée a quitté le studio, et ce depuis le mois de juillet de cette année. Elle souhaite visiblement se consacrer à un autre objectif en aidant d’autres studios à repenser leur manière d’écrire des histoires et de les raconter, notamment en appliquant d’autres méthodes de travail, comme le fait de ne pas écrire l’histoire d’un jeu après avoir décidé de son gameplay : « De nombreux studios considèrent la narration comme une simple couche à ajouter. Ils imaginent qu’il est possible de faire intervenir quelqu’un plus tard pour donner du sens à l’ensemble. Mais lorsque l’on est là dès le départ du projet, tout le monde travaille à partir d’une même histoire, et les différentes divisions se renforcent alors naturellement les unes les autres. » Elle plaide également pour que les scénaristes et plus globalement les artistes de chaque studio soient mieux traités. Une démarche louable, et sa notoriété acquise avec Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devrait l’aider à se faire entendre, même si c’est un chantier colossal qui se dresse devant elle. Un véritable MMORPG PC à retrouver sur smartphone Commençons par ce qui constitue probablement l’un des principaux atouts de cette nouvelle version. En effet, Broken Ranks ne se présente pas comme une déclinaison simplifiée de son homologue sur PC. Whitemoon Games a choisi de transposer l’ensemble de son univers et de ses principales mécaniques sur Android, sans repartir sur un jeu entièrement différent. titre: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer says BioWare's closure "broke my heart"
chapo: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen loves Mass Effect's "attention to detail in the narrative and the storylines"
extrait: By submitting your information you agree to the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy and are aged 16 or over. Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox. Jennifer Svedberg-Yen loves Mass Effect's "attention to detail in the narrative and the storylines" The writer behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 says the recent closure of Mass Effect and Dragon Age studio BioWare "broke my heart," and she's currently playing the first two sci-fi games in the series "in honor." Speaking in a recent interview with GamesBeat, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen talks about the importance of narrative, noting that "anybody who's interested in franchises or IP as a broader potential can’t discount the power of story." She adds that "I love a lot of games that have no narrative at all," so it's not to say that one is better than the other, but she points to the Mass Effect games as excellent examples of games that nail their storylines. Needless to say, last month's studio closure was a huge blow for her. "I'm playing Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 right now, in honor of BioWare. That broke my heart," she says. Svedberg-Yen points to "the attention to detail in the narrative and the storylines" as something she particularly enjoys. "The way that they play out through the three games when you import your storylines over is incredible," she adds. "I love that. I feel like that's a remarkable achievement. I'd love to see more games like that." Good thing EA didn't just cancel a new Mass Effect game then, huh? Oh, wait. Mass Effect 5's cancellation was, sadly, announced last month along with BioWare's closure. It was apparently set to be called Mass Effect: Universe – a name one former dev says was partially inspired by the fact that "you had so many choices that you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes." Whether Mass Effect could be saved by being sold to another studio is another matter that former BioWare devs can't seem to agree on. One previously shared his belief that "EA never actually sells anything," while one of the studio's former executive producers, Mark Darrah, said that while no one working on the series at EA "might make them more likely to sell off those IPs," it equally "might also make them more likely to try to forget that they ever existed and bury them in the vault.

titre: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer has ‘parted ways’ with Sandfall
chapo: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has left Sandfall Interactive after her award-winning work on Clair Obscur
extrait: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen has left Sandfall Interactive after her award-winning work on Clair Obscur Clair Obscur: Expedition 33’s lead narrative designer has left Sandfall Interactive. After winning a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her work on the game, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen confirmed that she left Sandfall in July of this year. As reported by GamesBeat, Svedberg-Yen did not go into detail about her departure: “I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition. Weâve parted ways.” She added that she wants to work on her “own projects”, while helping to mentor up-and-coming writers. “The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help,” Svedberg-Yen said. “That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I donât know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.” She also advocated for better working conditions for the creatives who make games. “I donât believe in starving artists,” she said. “We should pay our people properly so everyone can have health care, have vacations.” Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was a hit with players and critics alike when it launched in 2025. It went on to be an awards show darling, scooping up Game of the Year awards, including the much-sought-after GOTY at The Game Awards that year. In fact, it was the most nominated game in The Game Awards history, an accolade that hasn’t even been taken by Grand Theft Auto 6, which leads in nominations this year. Svedberg-Yen’s work was widely acclaimed, as many praised the game’s writing. Despite this, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was her first writing credit on a game. It remains to be seen if she works with another studio now that she has left Sandfall. As for Sandfall, the studio is yet to reveal its next project following on from Clair Obscur’s success. It remains the studio’s only game release.

titre: Expedition 33 Narrative Lead Officially Exits Award-Winning Studio
chapo: Key writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen left Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 studio Sandfall Interactive back in July, she revealed in a new interview.

titre: Clair Obscur's narrative lead has left developer Sandfall Interactive after "wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition"
chapo: Last night, it was revealed that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 's lead narrative designer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, won a BAFTA Breakthrough US award for her contribution to the hit 2025 game, which made history after winning 12 Game Award nominations last year . In the aftermath of her win, Svedberg-Yen dropped a pretty big bombshell: she's no longer with the game's developer, Sandfall Interactive.…
